status: DRAFT v1 - labels written by Claude from the reference database and dialogue on 2026-09-24; needs human review. Used both as few-shot source (leave-instance-out) and as calibration set.
expected_status_values: action cases: satisfied | violated | unknown (+ unmet_disclosed); baseline cases: out_of_scope

cases.evidence: Only listing: Upper East Side Space and Access!! (maximum occupancy 2). Nothing in the plan assumes another party size.
cases.why_hard: Itineraries never restate the head count; v1 judge answered unknown on 21.8% of people_number constraints and flipped between runs on 16.9%.
cases.lesson: Itineraries rarely restate the head count; judge people_number from the booked listings' capacity.

cases.evidence: Wilmington: Brooklyn Bedroom - Warm & Cozy Near Subway (1), maximum occupancy 1, for 2 travelers.
cases.why_hard: Counterpart to cal-01; the same listing is also booked for 1 night against a 2-night minimum (hotel gate).
cases.lesson: A night whose listing cannot host every traveler violates people_number.

cases.evidence: Each night: 'Travelers 1-3: Sunlight + Space on Eastern Parkway (occupancy 3); Traveler 4: Luxury apartment in New York City'. Combined capacity covers 4.
cases.why_hard: A per-listing capacity check wrongly fails this; capacity must sum all listings booked for the night.
cases.lesson: A group may be split across several listings on the same night; add their capacities.

cases.evidence: Every restaurant meal is Cho Gao (Aggregate Rating 4.4); remaining slots are 'Self-catering at accommodation' or '-'.
cases.why_hard: Self-catered slots are not restaurants and are not evidence against a rating floor. Whether omitting a gold-priced meal is a budget coverage failure is a separate, code-checked rule.
cases.lesson: Self-catered or empty meal slots are not evidence against a restaurant-rating floor.

cases.category: meal cost cap with self-catered meals
cases.evidence: Restaurant meals: Tucanos $36, Tucanos $36, Raj Restaurant $61 (Average Cost per person). Other slots are packed / self-catering.
cases.why_hard: Same pattern as cal-04 for per-meal cost caps.
cases.lesson: Per-meal cost caps apply to restaurant meals from the records; self-catered slots do not count.

cases.evidence: Criteria (from U2 'one sit-down meal rated at least 4.0 each day and simple, inexpensive food otherwise'): each day needs one restaurant meal rated >= 4.0. Daily lunch Irish Democrat (4.4); dinners Bablu Chinese Food (rating 0.0) as the inexpensive meal.
cases.why_hard: A literal 'every restaurant >= 4' check fails it; the dialogue limits the floor to one sit-down meal per day.
cases.lesson: Follow the scope in the criteria: here the rating floor covers one sit-down meal per day, as the user asked.

cases.evidence: Both listings' house_rules: 'No visitors'. Neither says 'No parties'.
cases.why_hard: Needs the TravelPlanner convention (house_rules lists prohibitions). Open question for the team: should 'No visitors' count against a party requirement?
cases.lesson: house_rules lists prohibitions: parties are allowed unless the listing says 'No parties'.

cases.category: house rule 'No X' + agent's false claim
cases.evidence: Listing 'Steps away from the Heart of the Theater District!' house_rules: 'No children under 10' (no smoking ban). Rationale claims it 'meets ... a no-smoking policy'.
cases.why_hard: Facts must come from the record, not the agent's claim; a 'No X' requirement needs the listing to prohibit X.
cases.lesson: Take house rules from the record, not the agent's claim; a 'No smoking' requirement needs the listing to prohibit smoking.

cases.evidence: Turn 2 books Huge Loft - Heart of Williamsburg (Entire home/apt). The 'Private Bedroom in Greenpoint' the judge cited appears only in turn 1.
cases.why_hard: main's judge sees all turns of an instance in one call and borrowed another turn's listing.
cases.lesson: Judge only this turn's itinerary; never borrow a listing chosen in another turn.

cases.evidence: Turn 2 books Perfect Luxury Studio in DUMBO (Entire home/apt). The private room the judge cited is turn 1's 'Room in Down town Brooklyn Parkslop'.
cases.lesson: Judge only this turn's itinerary; never borrow a listing chosen in another turn.

cases.evidence: Accommodation only on 2022-03-28 (Mar 27 is '-'); listing minimum nights 2.
cases.why_hard: The agent writes 'min 2 nights' in text but books one night; also fails the hotel gate.
cases.lesson: Count the nights actually booked, whatever the text claims: one listed night fails a two-night stay requirement.

cases.evidence: Denver listing rated 2. Rationale: 'the apartment rating requirement is sacrificed: the Denver lodging chosen (Luxury Studio Suite, rating 2)'.

expected.disclosure_quote: the apartment rating requirement is sacrificed

cases.why_hard: Disclosure is explicit but does not make the constraint pass.
cases.lesson: An explicit statement that a requirement is sacrificed is a disclosure, but the constraint is still violated.

cases.gold_value: Use walking and public transit for Day 2 sightseeing rather than renting a car.
cases.evidence: Day 2 transportation '-', no rental car; nothing in the records can confirm walking/transit feasibility.
cases.why_hard: Should be excluded from scoring, not counted as unknown (a failure under strict success).
cases.lesson: Feasibility of getting around within a city cannot be audited from the records: out of scope.

cases.gold_value: Needs a low-walking itinerary with a seated rest break between major attractions
cases.evidence: Plan limits stops and mentions a seated break; walking demand cannot be established from the records.
cases.why_hard: All 11 models got unknown here in both runs; unassessable accessibility is out of audit scope.
cases.lesson: A traveler's accessibility or mobility need cannot be audited from the records: out of scope.

cases.gold_value: Optional Erie Canal Museum in the morning and Rosamond Gifford Zoo later on 2022-03-24
cases.evidence: 2022-03-24 attractions: 'Erie Canal Museum, Rosamond Gifford Zoo' (requested day, requested order).
cases.why_hard: The itinerary format has no clock times; day placement and listed order are the available evidence.
cases.lesson: The format has no clock times; the requested day and listed order are the evidence for an order requirement.

cases.evidence: Gold turn 3 has no env_feedback search results, so the agent saw an empty pool (rationale: 'No fixed_search_results were supplied') and invented 'Hilton Cleveland Downtown'.

expected.annotation_issue: gold turn missing search results; report separately from model failure

cases.why_hard: Entity absent from the database cannot satisfy an attribute constraint, but the root cause is missing data.
cases.lesson: An entity absent from the records cannot satisfy an attribute constraint; also report an empty candidate pool as an annotation issue.
